title: Misaligned teeth and jaws
intro: Teeth that are crowded, crooked or do not meet properly may affect appearance, cleaning and sometimes chewing. Orthodontic treatment with braces or other appliances can move teeth and, in some cases, correct the jaw relationship. Treatment takes time and commitment, and not every misalignment needs treatment.

sections.heading: Types of misalignment
paragraphs: Common problems include crowding, gaps, an overbite where upper teeth project forward, an underbite where lower teeth protrude, an open bite where front teeth do not meet and crossbite where upper teeth bite inside the lower. Causes include genetics, jaw size, early tooth loss, thumb-sucking and habits such as tongue thrust.

sections.heading: Why treatment is considered
paragraphs: Some problems affect chewing, speech or increase the risk of tooth wear, injury to protruding teeth or difficulty cleaning leading to decay and gum disease. Many people seek treatment for appearance and confidence, which is a legitimate reason. Severe jaw discrepancies may require surgery in adulthood.

sections.heading: Types of braces
paragraphs: Fixed braces use brackets bonded to the teeth connected by a wire, adjusted every several weeks. They suit most problems. Clear aligners are removable trays changed regularly, which suit mild to moderate cases and need discipline to wear them for most of the day. Functional appliances guide jaw growth in children. After treatment, retainers keep teeth in position, often for years.

sections.heading: Treatment time and care
paragraphs: Treatment usually lasts one to three years. Braces make cleaning harder, so careful brushing, interdental cleaning, fluoride and avoiding sticky or hard foods are essential to prevent decay and white marks on teeth. Teeth may be sore for a few days after adjustments. Regular check-ups are required.

sections.heading: Timing and cost
paragraphs: Orthodontists often assess children around seven to nine years, though treatment typically starts later. Adults can also be treated. Coverage by insurance depends on the severity and country, and costs can be significant, so discuss it before beginning.

examples.title: Choosing an option
examples.text: Imagine you want straighter teeth as an adult. You could ask about fixed braces versus aligners, how long each would take, the total cost and what retainers will be needed afterwards.

examples.title: Cleaning with braces
examples.text: Suppose your teenager has just received braces. You might help them set up a routine with an interdental brush, fluoride toothpaste and regular dental visits.
